text:
maya: Heads-up — eu-west cluster saw a 3x tail latency spike at ~20:05. Dashboards point to one tenant causing KV cache thrash + egress microbursts. Anyone oncall?
dan: I'm on. Seeing the same on allocator + egress graphs. Dedicated pools look stable.
ops-bot: alert: eu-west.p99_latency > 300ms (20:05) https://metrics.redwood/example/alerts/12345
sara: Noisy neighbor candidate: tenant t-214, lots of small parallel requests in bursts.
liam: Could be that new quantized model hitting long context lengths -> big KV churn. Memory pressure caused slab evictions.
maya: Ran a quick sim of per-slice queue-capping (soft qcap) in a small canary; p99 improved ~40%.
dan: Can you paste the numbers?
maya: ```
canary: qcap=100 -> p99=220ms -> cost +2%
baseline: qcap=inf -> p99=360ms -> cost baseline
qcap=50 -> p99=250ms -> cost +6%
```
sara: Nice improvement. Concern: capping increases warm-pool churn -> more cold starts.
liam: Correct. My sims show cold-start token cost up ~1.8%, but net SLA wins.
maya: Proposal: "harmony" flow = per-tenant soft-queue-cap + eviction-backoff + automatic soft-evac to dedicated for top offenders. Start eu-west canary.
dan: How do we tie to routing? auto-route to dedicated for tagged noisy tenants?
jordan: Suggestion: tag tenants noisy=true -> routing policy moves traffic to dedicated or throttles concurrency.
sara: Dedicated adds fixed $; need a cost vs SLA penalty calc.
maya: Quick napkin: moving top 5 noisy tenants in eu-west -> +$12k/month dedicated cost; estimated avoided SLO penalties ~$30k/mo (based on recent incidents).
liam: If dedicated fills, fallback is routing to quantized-compatible model in another region or degrade gracefully — higher latency but keeps service alive.
dan: We should formalize a graceful evac runbook (notify -> create slice -> shift -> monitor -> rollback).
maya: Draft runbook snippet: ```
- step1: tag tenant: noisy=yes
- step2: provision dedicated-slice(size=2) and wait 5m
- step3: apply qcap=80 on default slice
- step4: shift 50% traffic: `curl -X POST /route/shift -d '{"tenant":"t-214","percent":50}'`
- step5: monitor p99, kv_evictions/sec, egress_bytes
- step6: if p99>350ms -> rollback to previous route
```
sara: Add steps to notify account team + billing team and open a postmortem ticket if evac occurs.
ops-bot: deploy-candidate created by maya -> https://deploys.redwood/candidates/789
dan: Plan: run 2h canary tonight at 23:00 UTC. Alerts: p99 increase OR dedicated provision cost > budget threshold.
maya: I'll own the runbook PR and the canary. @sara validate the billing calc? @liam sanity-check cold-start delta?
sara: on it. I'll post a short spreadsheet.
liam: running sims now, ETA ~2h.
jordan: Also propose an automated circuit: if kv_evictions/sec > 100 for 2m then auto-trigger soft-evac (provision + qcap + 30% shift).
dan: Ack, add to alerting/playbook.
maya: Tagging to ops backlog. TL;DR: per-slice queue-caps + soft eviction -> big p99 win, small net cost; canary 23:00 UTC tonight.
sara: :thumbsup:
dan: :shipit:
ops-bot: canary scheduled for 23:00 UTC (eu-west) — will post summary at end of run
